comment: One schema for agent session links, so an emitter and a parser cannot drift. The web fallback page (https://cmux.com/deeplink/agent?harness=&session=&host=&name=&message=) and the native link cmux NEXT opens (cmux://agent/<harness>/<session>?host=&name=&message=) carry the same parameters. harness and session address the session; host names the machine it runs on; name is its callsign; message names one message to scroll to and highlight; machine is the hint every kind of cmux link takes. A link is an address, not a credential. Consumers: web/app/[locale]/(landing)/deeplink/[kind]/deeplink-agent.ts (web/tests/deeplink-agent.test.ts) and the app's parser, Packages/macOS/CmuxNext/Sources/CmuxNextActions/DeepLink (Tests/CmuxNextActionsTests/AgentLinkSchemaTests.swift), and acpmux's reader behind `acpmux resolve`, cmux-tui/crates/acpmux/src/agent_link.rs. All three run the vectors below, so none can drift from this file.
queryOrder: queryParams is the order every emitter writes the query in, so the same chat is always the same link (DeepLink.url writes the hints, then machine).
ignoredOrder: The names a reader reports as ignored: the optional parameters above, in the order `params` lists them, then every name no agent link reads, in the order the URL carries them; each name once. How they are shown is the reader's: the page prints an unknown name inside the charset a name may have (32 characters, `?` for a name with nothing printable left) and stops after eight, so no URL text is echoed, and the app's toast caps its text. The page reads a parsed form, not the URL, so among its unknown names one written only in digits comes first, whatever the URL's order; and a stray name it prints as a parameter the link did use is dropped unsaid, rather than denying a parameter the link carries.
valuelessParams: A parameter written with no `=` at all (`?machine`), and one with an empty value (`?host=`), name nothing: both readers name them ignored and open the chat. The page cannot tell the two apart (a form never does), so neither does this schema. On the other kinds of link, which this file does not describe, a valueless parameter stays what it always was.

harness.comment: An acpmux harness family: claude, codex, opencode, ... (DeepLink.isHarness)

machine.comment: The machine the target lives on, which every kind of cmux link takes (DeepLink.machine). A hint: ids are globally unique.

host.comment: The machine the session runs on, as cmux names it.

name.comment: The session's callsign, shown as its human name.

message.comment: One assistant message of the session's transcript, as the harness itself ids it: the ACP `agent_message_chunk.messageId` the page keys its rows by (Claude Code writes `msg_...`). The chat scrolls to that message and marks it. A link naming anything else -- a prompt, a tool call, a Cloud row id, an id this machine's transcript never saw -- opens the chat and leaves the view where it is.
